overview:
This private 3-day tour is the most direct way to see the real Sahara from Fes and still come back to the same city. In three days you cross the cedar forests of the Middle Atlas, ride a camel into the tallest dunes in Morocco, sleep in a desert camp in Erg Chebbi, walk between the 300-metre walls of the Todra Gorge and spend a night in the Dades valley before driving home through the high plateaus.

It is a road trip as much as a desert trip, and we want you to know that before you book: the drives are long (about 7 to 9 hours a day including stops), because Merzouga is roughly 470 km from Fes. In return you see a huge range of landscapes in a short time, with a private driver who stops whenever you want for photos, tea or a stretch.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 3 days, 2 nights
• Start and finish: your riad or hotel in Fes
• Type: private tour – only your group in the vehicle
• Vehicle: air-conditioned 4x4 or minivan depending on group size
• Nights: 1 night in a desert camp in Erg Chebbi (Merzouga), 1 night in a hotel or kasbah in the Dades valley
• Meals included: 2 breakfasts and 2 dinners
• Activity level: easy; the camel ride and the gorge walk are gentle
• Best months: October to May; summer is possible with early starts

WHY THIS ROUTE WORKS
Most desert trips from Fes go to Merzouga and come straight back the same way. This loop returns by a different road: after the dunes you head west to the Todra Gorge and the Dades valley, so the second day shows you canyons, oases and kasbahs instead of the same road twice. You see two of the great landscapes of southern Morocco – sand sea and red-rock gorges – in one short trip.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Travellers based in Fes with only a few days, couples and friends who want the camel-and-camp experience, families with children who are fine with long drives, and photographers who want sunset and sunrise in the dunes.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If long drives are hard for you, consider [our 3-day Fes to Merzouga tour with two nights in the desert area](/en-US/morocco/fes/tours/3-days-fes-to-merzouga-desert-tour-two-nights-in-the-sahara/ef9e89754f81897c29489983), or a 4-day tour that spreads the driving over more days. If you want to end in Marrakech instead of Fes, choose [our 3-day Fes to Marrakech desert tour](/en-US/morocco/fes/tours/3-day-desert-tour-from-fes-to-marrakech-via-merzouga-and-the-dades-valley/c70d8bc6c601ca15f9992e4b).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Bring a small overnight bag for the camp: your main luggage stays safely in the vehicle. Pack a warm layer – desert nights are cold from November to March, sometimes close to freezing – plus sunglasses, sun cream, a scarf against wind and sand, and a torch or phone light. Camps have beds, blankets and toilets; standard camps may have shared facilities, luxury camps have private bathrooms. Mobile signal is usually available but weak in the dunes.
descriptions:
Today is the great crossing: in one day you leave the green north of Morocco and arrive at the edge of the Sahara. The landscapes change almost every hour – from olive groves and cedar forests to high bare plateaus, from the palm-filled Ziz valley to the first orange dunes – and the day ends in the most memorable way possible, on a camel walking into the sand as the sun goes down.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates and shift with the season and your pace)
07:30 – Pick-up at your riad or hotel in Fes. Your driver helps with luggage if your riad is inside the medina.
08:30 – Ifrane: short stop (20–30 min) for photos and coffee in the alpine-style town nicknamed the “Switzerland of Morocco”, with its well-known stone lion.
09:15 – Cedar forest near Azrou: stop (about 20 min) to see the Barbary macaques.
11:30 – Midelt: lunch break (about 1 hour, lunch not included).
13:00 – Ziz gorges and the Ziz valley viewpoint (short photo stop, 15 min).
14:30 – Errachidia and Erfoud: drive on, with a tea or fuel stop.
16:30 – Arrival in Merzouga at the edge of the dunes. Leave your main bags in the vehicle.
17:00 – Camel ride into Erg Chebbi (about 1 to 1.5 hours), timed to reach a dune for sunset.
18:30 – Arrival at the desert camp, mint tea, settle into your tent.
20:00 – Dinner at the camp, then Berber music around the fire and stargazing.

Total driving: about 470 km, usually 7.5 to 8.5 hours with stops.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The camel ride is gentle, but if you have back problems or prefer not to ride, the camp can be reached by 4x4 – tell us when booking.
• Sunset time changes a lot through the year (from around 18:00 in winter to after 20:00 in summer); your driver adjusts the departure so you arrive in time.
• In summer, the hottest part of the afternoon is spent driving in the air-conditioned vehicle, and the camel ride starts later.
• Wear closed shoes or sandals you can easily empty: the sand is soft and gets into everything.

INCLUDED TODAY: pick-up in Fes, private transport, bottled water, camel ride, night in the desert camp, dinner.
NOT INCLUDED TODAY: lunch in Midelt, drinks, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: on rare days of strong wind or sandstorm, the camel ride may be shortened or replaced by a 4x4 transfer to the camp for safety. In winter, snow sometimes closes the Middle Atlas road near Ifrane for a few hours; the driver then takes the alternative road via Sefrou or waits for it to reopen.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the feeling of having crossed a whole country in one day – and the silence of the dunes after the engine stops.

Day two begins with the most beautiful light of the trip – sunrise over the Sahara – and then turns west along the old caravan and oasis road. You visit the market town of Rissani, walk inside the Todra Gorge, and end the day in the Dades valley, a canyon of red rock and mud-brick kasbahs. It's a day of contrasts: sand in the morning, stone canyons in the afternoon.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
06:00–07:00 – Wake-up call and short climb to a dune for sunrise (time depends on season).
07:30 – Breakfast at the camp.
08:15 – Return by camel or 4x4 to Merzouga, shower available at a partner hotel or auberge, collect your luggage.
09:30 – Drive to Rissani (about 40 min).
10:15 – Rissani: short visit and walk (30–45 min), market days are especially lively.
11:00 – Drive west via Alnif or Erfoud–Tinejdad (about 2.5–3 hours with a stop).
13:30 – Lunch in Tinghir area (not included).
14:45 – Todra Gorge: walk through the narrowest section (about 45 min–1 hour).
16:00 – Drive to the Dades valley via Boumalne Dades (about 1–1.5 hours).
17:30 – Arrival at your hotel or kasbah in the Dades valley, free time.
19:30 – Dinner at the hotel.

Total driving: about 300 km, usually 5.5 to 6.5 hours with stops.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Sunrise is cold in winter: keep your warm layer and scarf with you.
• The Todra walk is on flat ground along the river; good shoes help but no hiking skills are needed.
• Rissani's main market days are traditionally Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday; on other days the town is quieter.

INCLUDED TODAY: breakfast, return from camp, private transport, water, night in the Dades valley, dinner.
NOT INCLUDED TODAY: lunch, drinks, optional local guide in the Tinghir palm grove, tips.

ALTERNATIVES: after rain, the Todra riverbed can be wet – the walk then stays on the road side. In very hot weather the gorge walk is moved to later afternoon when the canyon is in shade.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the change from soft dunes to vertical rock in a single day – and a sense of how oasis life works in the south.

The last day is the long drive home, and we want to be honest: it's the longest driving day of the tour. But it is not empty time. The road climbs from the Dades valley across wide, empty plateaus where nomad tents and flocks are still part of the landscape, passes Midelt beneath the High Atlas, and ends back in the cedar forests and green hills of the Middle Atlas. Your driver keeps the stops flexible so the day stays comfortable.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
07:30 – Breakfast at your hotel.
08:15 – Departure from the Dades valley, heading east and north.
10:30 – Coffee or tea stop (about 20 min).
12:30 – Midelt: lunch break (about 1 hour, not included).
14:00 – Drive across the Middle Atlas via Zeida and Azrou (about 2.5–3 hours).
16:30 – Optional short stop in Ifrane or the cedar forest if you missed it on Day 1.
17:30–18:30 – Arrival at your riad or hotel in Fes.

Total driving: about 450–550 km depending on the road, usually 8 to 9 hours with stops.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Keep snacks and water in the car; services are sparse on the high plateaus.
• If you have a flight from Fes, book it for the following day – this day can run late with traffic or weather.
• Tell your driver if you would like more stops: there is no fixed programme today.

INCLUDED TODAY: breakfast, private transport, water, drop-off in Fes.
NOT INCLUDED TODAY: lunch, drinks, tips.

ALTERNATIVES: in winter, if snow is forecast on the Middle Atlas passes, the driver may change the route or leave earlier. If you prefer a shorter last day, ask about ending the tour in Marrakech instead (similar distance but different scenery) or adding a night in Midelt.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the scale of Morocco – you will have travelled more than 1,000 km and seen sand, canyons, plateaus and forests in three days.

faq.question: How long are the drives on this tour?
faq.answer: Merzouga is about 470 km from Fes. Day 1 usually takes 7.5 to 8.5 hours including stops, Day 2 about 5.5 to 6.5 hours, and Day 3 is the longest at 8 to 9 hours. These are estimates and depend on traffic, weather and how many stops you want.

faq.question: Is this a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Only your group travels in the vehicle, with your own driver. You choose when to stop for photos, tea or meals.

faq.question: What kind of desert camp will we stay in?
faq.answer: You choose Standard or Luxury when booking. Standard camps have beds, blankets and toilets (sometimes shared); Luxury camps have larger tents with private bathrooms and hot showers. Both include dinner and breakfast.

faq.question: Is the camel ride suitable for children and older travellers?
faq.answer: Yes for most people. The camels walk slowly and a cameleer leads them. Very young children ride with an adult. If anyone in your group has back or hip problems, the camp can be reached by 4x4 instead.

faq.question: What should I pack for the desert night?
faq.answer: A small overnight bag with a warm layer (nights can be very cold in winter), sun cream, sunglasses, a scarf, a phone light and any medication. Your main luggage stays locked in the vehicle.

faq.question: Which meals are included?
faq.answer: Dinner and breakfast each night (2 dinners and 2 breakfasts). Lunches and drinks are not included, so you can choose where and what to eat.

faq.question: Can the tour end in Marrakech instead of Fes?
faq.answer: Yes, as a different itinerary: [our 3-day Fes to Marrakech desert tour](/en-US/morocco/fes/tours/3-day-desert-tour-from-fes-to-marrakech-via-merzouga-and-the-dades-valley/c70d8bc6c601ca15f9992e4b) goes from Fes through Merzouga and the Dades valley to Marrakech.

faq.question: When is the best time to do this tour?
faq.answer: October to May is the most comfortable period. Summer (June to September) is very hot in the desert in the afternoon, so we start early and ride camels later. Winter is sunny by day but cold at night, and snow can occasionally affect the Middle Atlas roads.

faq.question: Is there Wi-Fi or electricity at the camp?
faq.answer: Most camps have electricity (often solar) for lights and phone charging. Wi-Fi is limited or absent; mobile data usually works but can be weak among the dunes.

faq.question: Can you pick us up at Fes airport?
faq.answer: Yes. If you land in the morning, your driver can meet you at Fes–Saïss airport and start the tour straight away; the first day then runs a little later. At the end of Day 3 we can drop you at the airport, but because the last day is long we recommend flying out the following day.

faq.question: Can we add sandboarding, quad biking or a visit to Khamlia?
faq.answer: Yes. Sandboards are often available at the camp for a short try on the dunes. Quad biking and buggy rides around Merzouga are optional extras paid locally, and a short stop in Khamlia to hear Gnawa music can be added on the morning of Day 2 if you leave the camp early. Tell us when booking so your driver can plan the timing.

faq.question: Do you cater for vegetarian or other diets?
faq.answer: Yes. Hotels and camps prepare vegetarian meals, and most other diets or allergies can be handled if you tell us when booking. Moroccan dinners are usually soup, salads, a tagine or couscous and fruit, so a vegetable version is easy to make.

faq.question: Can we spend more time in the desert?
faq.answer: Yes. If you would rather have a full day around Merzouga instead of the Todra and Dades loop, choose [our 3-day Fes to Merzouga tour with two nights in the desert area](/en-US/morocco/fes/tours/3-days-fes-to-merzouga-desert-tour-two-nights-in-the-sahara/ef9e89754f81897c29489983). You can also add a night to this tour; ask us and we will adjust the plan.
